title: fix(codex): preserve sandboxed process inspection and setup errors
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex turns failing when a macOS sandbox refuses to execute `/bin/ps`, and zero-config setup silently treating Codex detection or process-inspection errors as absence and selecting Ollama.

## User Impact

Sandboxed Bun runtimes can reuse an existing Codex login without allowing `ps` execution. Setup keeps detection and inspection failures visible. Genuine absence, sign-in-required behavior, and fallback after ordinary model failures remain covered. Shipped v2026.10.4 contains the old snapshot path, so existing users under rejecting sandboxes are affected. No credential migration or proc-safe release is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

One core Darwin owner now supplies Codex snapshots and process-group census through the documented `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime` contract. Bun uses libproc for topology/start identity and the pinned proc-safe reader for arguments. Node has no FFI and the pinned package has no Darwin census API, so Node retains bounded `ps` inspection and its topology-only group projection. Normalized UTC start identities remain compatible with persisted Codex registrations.

Darwin restricts full start-time records across UIDs. Collect complete short-record topology, then read full identities only for relevant Codex roots/descendants and the observer. Relevant denials stay errors. The retained PR-tooling inventory includes the new core dependency.

## Evidence

- 178 process/census/Codex snapshot tests pass (29.22 s wall), 20 automatic-setup tests pass (44.07 s), and 19 extracted-wrapper/import-closure tests pass (43.10 s). Detection probes, inference detection, and credential metadata add 39 passing tests (48.61 s / 82.62 s / 3.83 s).
- Production build passes (244.50 s); SDK exports, qualified Codex import profile, targeted lint/types, and independent Codex review through P2 pass.
- Developer ID signed JIT standalone embeds the requested 77-plugin desktop set. Seatbelt explicitly denies `/bin/ps`; the real Codex plain turn returns exact `HR_OK`, exit 0, in 41.421 s. No physical loose CLI entry is present.
- A synthetic Codex metadata denial surfaces `Codex sign-in detection failed` with its permission error through the real `openclaw.setup.auto` RPC. No primary model is selected and no Ollama inference is attempted. Real loose Node v26.12.0 also returns exact `HR_OK` in 22.375 s.
- [Exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38917768570) passes, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. CI caught and verified repairs for the retained wrapper import, export-name collision, and Node census projection.

Local limitations are retained: repository-wide max-lines, wrapper-shadowing, and dead-export findings reproduce on the inspected clean-main snapshot. One macOS-only PR-tooling warm/sparse test exceeds its existing 120-second deadline both in the full file and in isolation; 15 other provisioning cases pass. No timeout or baseline was weakened. All OpenClaw proof state is isolated; real Codex auth uses `homeScope=user` REUSE with no OAuth copies.

Related: #174147.
